transcript:
Header: 2026-06-30 15:00 UTC | Duration: 55m | Attendees: Jordan Lee, Priya Kapoor (Redwood); Alex Rivera, Maya Chen, Owen Park, Sasha Kim (Spectrum Data)

Summary (auto): POC scoping to define latency/throughput SLOs for Spectrum Data's conversational summarization pipeline. Decide TTFT vs TPOT targets, p95/p99 thresholds, workload sizing for benchmark, and measurement plan.

00:00 Alex Rivera: ok let's kick off, um, thanks everyone for joining. we're trying to scope the poc for the summarization endpoint, time to first token is our big concern plus cost.
00:12 Jordan Lee: yes thanks Alex, Jordan from Redwood, with Priya on the technical side. quick agenda: understand your workload, agree success criteria (TTFT vs TPOT and p95/p99), bench plan, and next steps. sound right?
00:25 Alex: yep, that covers it.
00:30 Maya Chen: just to add context, current infra: we run a microservice that proxies user prompts to a hosted model, average prompt length about 180 tokens, response about 320 tokens. about 150 RPS during peak across a small set of high-concurrency endpoints.
00:46 Owen Park: infra: k8s in our VPC, no public egress for some teams, we prefer dedicated or private deployment for compliance.
00:55 Jordan: good context. for SLOs, do you currently measure TTFT (time to first token) or TPOT (time to produced token / total generation)?
01:05 Maya: we currently only look at total response time at the app layer, which is closer to TPOT, but product wants fast start-of-response for perceived latency — so TTFT is actually the main UX metric.
01:18 Priya Kapoor: that makes sense, TTFT is more sensitive to model warm-up and KV cache behavior. TPOT/p99 matters for throughput planning and cost.
01:28 Sasha Kim: product target: perceived snappiness of chat — goal is first token under 250ms p95 and under 450ms p99. Is that realistic?
01:38 Priya: depends on deployment. On hosted we can get aggressive TTFT with small context and streaming, but tail depends on model variant and sequence length. Dedicated/private has more control but needs right GPU sizing.
01:49 Jordan: can I restate? Proposed success criteria we should validate in the POC: TTFT p95 <= 250ms, TTFT p99 <= 450ms, sustained throughput 150 RPS with average generation length ~320 tokens and p95 token throughput (TPOT) consistent with 99% of requests completing within app-level 1.2s. Does that capture product ask?
02:10 Alex: yes that's close. One nuance: some enterprise customers use longer prompts up to 800 tokens; we'd like the SLO to be measured on two profiles: normal (180/320) and longtail (800/700).
02:26 Priya: good — we'll set up two workload profiles in the benchmark harness. We'll also capture cold-start vs warm KV cache.
02:35 Maya: can you explain how you measure TTFT and TPOT precisely? we want to align instrumentation.
02:42 Priya: sure. TTFT = timestamp at server receiving request to timestamp of first byte emitted by model stream. TPOT here we define as average per-token latency after the model begins generating; for bench we usually report p50/p95/p99 of TTFT and p50/p95/p99 token inter-arrival (token RT) and total end-to-end (request received to final token).
03:00 Owen: how do you factor in network and client-side? we have additional CDN + proxy hops.
03:06 Jordan: bench plan isolates model-serving latency by running the harness in the same region and capturing raw server-side timings, but we'll also run an end-to-end pass from your VPC to capture real-world app-level numbers. We'll provide both sets.
03:18 Alex: ok. timeline?
03:21 Jordan: propose: 1) this week - spectrum provides traces and sample requests; 2) Redwood builds harness and baseline config (Priya) 3) POC benchmark week of 2026-07-13 where we run hosted and a Dedicated config in parallel and collect metrics 4) analysis and follow-up week of 2026-07-20.
03:38 Sasha: cost sensitivity: if Dedicated required, we need ballpark monthly cost to justify.
03:44 Priya: we'll include a rough cost model for Dedicated sizing.\n
04:05 Priya: about measurement specifics: we'll run three modes for each profile — cold (empty KV cache), warm (population of typical prefixes), and production-simulated (mixed arrival patterns) — and produce p50/p95/p99 for TTFT, token inter-arrival, and end-to-end. We'll also report CPU/GPU utilization and memory to validate sizing.
04:28 Maya: for p95/p99 definitions, do you prefer absolute latency windows or relative to token position? our tail tends to spike on final tokens for long generations.
04:36 Priya: we will bucket by token position ranges (first token, first 50 tokens, last 50 tokens) and compute percentiles per bucket, so you can see tail behavior at start and end.
04:48 Alex: what's acceptable for TPOT p95 for us? product says total time should be under 1.2s 95% for normal payloads, but that seems tight for 320 tokens.
04:58 Jordan: clarify: we meant app-level 1.2s for smaller reference requests; for 320 tokens maybe our target is 1.2s per 100 tokens or we use tokens/sec. Let's define a token throughput metric: tokens/sec p95 >= 250 tps on normal profile, and p95 tokens/sec >= 200 tps on long profile.
05:14 Owen: those numbers help sizing. what GPUs do you recommend?
05:19 Priya: depends on model family. If you pick a 7B quantized model we can target 250-400 tps on an A10G-equivalent node with batching; for Llama-2-13B or similar, we recommend A100 or multiple A10Gs in a pool. We'll propose a baseline in the config doc.
05:33 Maya: about model variants: we use a tuned LLaMA-like open model currently; need to understand fallback and version pinning.
05:41 Jordan: Redwood supports model variants and automatic fallback; in the POC we'll keep version pinned and test fallback to a lower-capacity variant to validate graceful degradation.
05:50 Alex: security — we need SOC2, SSO/SAML integration, and ability to run Private in our VPC.
05:57 Jordan: noted; I'll send SOC2 summary and private deployment brief. For the POC benchmarking we can run Dedicated inside a customer VPC slice or run in Redwood's dedicated cluster with isolated network tunneling; we'll propose both options.
06:12 Sasha: logging and observability — we need per-request tracing and token-level timestamps in logs.
06:18 Priya: we'll enable tracing hooks and provide a sample trace format. We can also stream logs to your collector in the Private deployment.
06:26 Maya: what about measuring p99? our SLA enforcement will kick in at p99 so we need accurate tail measurement and confidence intervals.
06:34 Priya: we collect many samples and bootstrap confidence intervals. For p99 we recommend at least several thousand samples per profile to get stable estimates; we'll run sustained runs for 1-2 hours at peak RPS to capture tail.
06:48 Alex: acceptable duration. How do we handle burst traffic? we have short bursts up to 400 RPS.
06:55 Jordan: we'll include burst scenarios in the harness: 30s-2min peaks and observe queuing/latency. Redwood's Dedicated autoscaling and burst capacity options will be tested.
07:07 Owen: for private deployment, how much setup time do you expect?
07:12 Jordan: Private deploy takes longer: ~4-6 weeks for on-prem/VPC with configuration, but for POC we can emulate with Dedicated and IP allowlist faster.
07:21 Sasha: success criteria recap?
07:24 Jordan: proposed success criteria (to validate in POC): 1) TTFT p95 <= 250ms and p99 <= 450ms for normal profile (180/320) under 150 RPS steady-state; 2) token throughput p95 >= 250 tps (normal) and >=200 tps (long); 3) app-level end-to-end p95 <= 1.2s for short requests; 4) tail stability during bursts (peak 400 RPS) without >10% error rate or queueing-induced 2x latency increase.
07:54 Alex: that list is good but add the long-profile TTFT targets to be relaxed — p95 <= 600ms and p99 <= 1.2s for long requests.
08:04 Priya: ok we'll include that. We'll also produce a measurement plan doc that defines instrumentation keys and dashboards.
08:13 Maya: can you share the benchmark harness repo and traffic generator?
08:16 Priya: yes will share link, it's a simple k6 + custom streamer harness with token-level timers. link will be in the shared drive.
08:24 Jordan: next steps recap: Redwood to share harness + security docs + Dedicated sizing and cost estimate. Spectrum to share traces, sample requests, and confirm preferred deployment (Dedicated in Redwood cloud vs Private VPC).
08:36 Alex: can we also get a short runbook for test execution so our infra team can participate?
08:41 Priya: yes we'll include runbook and a checklist for network, certs, and sample data.
08:47 Sasha: one more ask — include a simple visualization of p95/p99 over time and per-token-position in the report.
08:54 Priya: will do.
09:01 Jordan: great. any other open questions?
09:03 Owen: nothing here.
09:05 Alex: no. thanks everyone.
09:07 Jordan: thanks — we'll follow up with artifacts.

End: 15:55 UTC

Notes on transcription: some speaker overlap and minor mis-transcriptions expected (model names, GPU SKU names sometimes abbreviated).
notes: POC focused on defining TTFT/TPOT targets, two workload profiles (normal, long), benchmark plan (cold/warm/production-simulated), burst scenarios, and measurement instrumentation. Security and Private/Dedicated deployment paths discussed.
